subtopic: Support-personnel ratio after a role change
stem: One Massachusetts pharmacist is supervising one certified pharmacy technician and two pharmacy technicians. Another employee holds a current pharmacy technician license but is assigned only to the front register and initially performs no professional pharmacy support. During a rush, the manager directs that employee to enter prescription data. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: While the employee performs only cashier duties and no professional pharmacy support, the employee may be excluded from the support-personnel ratio.
Once the employee begins prescription data entry, the cashier label no longer keeps the employee outside the ratio.
The resulting four-person support team is permitted because every member holds a pharmacy personnel credential.
The employee remains excluded for the entire shift because the schedule lists the employee as a cashier.
The data-entry assignment must satisfy technician scope and supervision rules independently of the numerical ratio analysis.

explanation.core_reasoning: Cashiers are excluded from the support-personnel ratio only while they are not supporting the pharmacist in a professional capacity. Prescription data entry changes the employee's actual function, so the employee can no longer be excluded merely because the schedule says cashier. Scope and supervision remain separate requirements. Here, adding an ordinary technician creates four support personnel with only one certified technician and no intern, which does not meet a permitted four-person composition.

choice_analysis.A: Correct: the exclusion applies while the employee is confined to cashier work and gives no professional support.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: prescription data entry is professional pharmacy support, so actual function defeats the cashier-only exclusion.
choice_analysis.C: Credentialing alone does not satisfy the composition rule for four support personnel; this group has only one certified technician and no intern.
choice_analysis.D: The regulation turns on the work actually performed, not the employee's scheduled title for the whole shift.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: being countable under a ratio does not itself authorize a task; the task must also be within technician scope and properly supervised.

related_facts: A pharmacist may supervise up to three support personnel if at least one is an intern or certified pharmacy technician.
A four-person configuration requires one certified technician and one intern, at least two certified technicians, or two interns.
explanation.mpje_trap: The cashier exclusion follows moment-to-moment function, while ratio composition and technician scope remain separate legal checks.

reasoning_steps: Classify the employee's actual function before and after reassignment
Recalculate the support-personnel count and test the four-person composition
Separately verify that prescription data entry is within the employee's licensed scope and supervision
